correctness.rationale: A finite change of the prime-weight set alters the integrated weight count only by an explicit multiple of log U plus an explicit constant. The extended Ingham corollary of Vernaeve--Vindas--Weiermann therefore gives an exact ratio: each deletion contributes kappa_m log(p) U^{-1/2}, and each addition contributes [kappa_m log(q)]^{-1} U^{1/2}. Multiplicative dependence reduces the distinct exponents to the numerical semigroup <u,v>, whose finite gap set has genus (u-1)(v-1)/2, yielding the dependent two-generator formula. Representative gap sets and constants were checked by exact arithmetic code.

originality.rationale: Golafshan arXiv:2609.19434v1 explicitly excludes multiplicatively dependent generators and gives (2,4) as a repeated-index example. The 2014 one-generator source supplies the analytic theorem but does not formulate the finite-prime perturbation law or dependent numerical-semigroup corollary. Exact and synonymous searches found no matching theorem. Residual uncertainty remains from a 2017 seminar announcement by Lenny Neyt whose complete mathematical scope was not available for inspection, and from the recency of the 2026 preprint.

value.rationale: The result treats the entire multiplicatively dependent complement to a new two-generator theorem, gives an explicit leading constant, and identifies the numerical-semigroup genus as the logarithmic penalty. The more general finite-prime perturbation transfer law is reusable for fixed finite modifications of sparse prime-index bases.
